title: Non-square matrices as dimension-changing linear transformations (3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra)
summary: This video explains the geometric meaning of non-square matrices as linear transformations between spaces of different dimensions. It shows that a matrix encodes a map by recording where the basis vectors land, with the matrix shape indicating input and output dimensions (e.g., a 3×2 matrix maps 2D input to 3D output; a 2×3 matrix maps 3D input to 2D output). The discussion introduces the column space as the image of the transformation (a plane through the origin in the output space) and covers the notion of full rank in the context of these maps. It also demonstrates a 2D-to-1D case encoded by a 1×2 matrix and hints at the connection to the dot product, inviting further exploration of transformations between differing dimensions.
topics: dot product relation (hinted for next video)

sections.title: Introduction: non-square matrices as dimension-changing linear transformations
sections.description: Sets up the idea of linear transformations between spaces of different dimensions and frames the question of what a non-square matrix means geometrically.

sections.title: Spaces and linearity: input vs output spaces
concepts: input space (2D) vs output space (3D or other)
sections.description: Distinguishes input and output spaces and emphasizes that linearity preserves parallel grid lines and maps the origin to the origin.

sections.title: Matrix encoding via images of basis vectors
sections.description: Illustrates how the matrix is constructed by recording where the input basis vectors land in the output space, yielding the matrix's columns.

sections.title: Interpreting a 3×2 matrix: 2D input to 3D output
concepts: rank = input dimension (full rank in this case)
sections.description: Explains that a 3×2 matrix encodes a map from two-dimensional input space to three-dimensional output space, with the column space forming a 2D plane through the origin.

sections.title: Interpreting a 2×3 matrix: 3D input to 2D output
sections.description: Shows the dual situation: a 2×3 matrix maps three-dimensional input to two-dimensional output, effectively projecting onto a 2D space.

sections.title: 2D to 1D transformation: 1×2 matrix
sections.description: Presents the case of mapping from two dimensions down to one, where the matrix has one row and two columns, yielding a scalar output per input basis vector.

sections.title: Connection to the dot product and upcoming discussion
sections.description: Notes the close ties between these transformations and the dot product, with a promise to explore that connection in the next video.

sections.title: Encouragement to explore transformations across dimensions
sections.description: Encourages active engagement with the ideas and invites the viewer to investigate transformations between different dimensional spaces on their own.
